newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to deal appropriately with forex swings - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to deal appropriately with forex swings - MOF.

text.p: Japan will deal appropriately with excessive movements in the foreign exchange market, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
Mitsuzuka said exchange rates should reflect fundamentals and that stability in the currency market is desirable for the Japanese economy.
"We will watch future movements carefully and also deal appropriately with excessive moves," Mitsuzuka said.

Speaking to the same committee, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said the authorities would be ready to intervene in foreign exchange markets if rates veered sharply from economic fundamentals.
"Intervention in the currency markets would be needed to ensure sustainable economic growth if exchange rates were to deviate substantially from economic fundamentals," Sakakibara said.
Currency intervention should not be carried out specifically out of consideration for the interests of individual and corporate investors, he added.
Asked about planned reforms of Japan's foreign exchange regulations, Sakakibara said Japan was unlikely to see a sudden flight of funds held by individual investors after deregulation.
But a substantial amount of individual investors' funds may flow out of Japan over the medium- and long-term in the wake of the reforms, he said.
